item.title: Topic Overview
item.description: Spiking Neural Networks A spiking neural network, or SNN, is a neural network that communicates through discrete spike events rather than continuously updated activation values.

item.title: Spiking Neural Networks
item.description: Spiking Neural Networks Learners will be able to explain why spiking neural networks are proposed as brain-inspired alternatives to conventional neural networks, describe spike-based computation and LIF neuron behavior, compare major SNN training strategies, interpret the source’s evaluation metrics...

item.title: 1.1 Why Spiking Neural Networks Exist
item.description: Why Spiking Neural Networks Exist Imagine a small camera on a battery-powered robot sitting in a hallway.

item.title: 1.2 Spikes, Timing, and Event-Driven Computation
item.description: Spikes, Timing, and Event-Driven Computation You already have the idea of an activation: a number that says how strongly a neuron-like unit is responding at a particular time step.

item.title: 1.3 Sparse Computation and Energy Awareness
item.description: Sparse Computation and Energy Awareness Imagine the spike train from the previous page arriving at a small battery-powered camera on a streetlight.

item.title: 1.4 The Leaky Integrate-and-Fire Neuron
item.description: The Leaky Integrate-and-Fire Neuron A spike event gives an SNN a compact way to say, “something happened at this time.” Now imagine one neuron receiving a stream of those events from earlier neurons.

item.title: 1.5 SNN Circuit Motifs
item.description: SNN Circuit Motifs Once a neuron can receive a spike train, let its internal state rise, and fire when it crosses a threshold, the next question is how many such neurons cooperate inside a network.
